headline: 49 Chinese military aircraft, 6 naval vessels, 6 official ships around Taiwan Mon-Tue, a 2026 single-day high
dek: Taiwan's defence ministry detected 49 Chinese military aircraft, six naval vessels and six official ships operating around Taiwan between Monday and Tuesday morning; 31 aircraft crossed into areas closer to Taiwan's main island. The 49 total is the highest single-day aircraft count of 2026 and the…
sources: Taiwan's defence ministry, reported by TaiwanPlus
fault_line: Routine pressure or a 2026-high signal -- does a record sortie day mean Beijing is turning up the heat, or just flying the same pattern louder?

sections.what_happened: Taiwan's defence ministry detected 49 Chinese military aircraft, six naval vessels and six official ships operating around Taiwan between Monday and Tuesday morning; 31 aircraft crossed into areas closer to Taiwan's main island. The 49 total is the highest single-day aircraft count of 2026 and the second-highest closer-approach count of the year, per TaiwanPlus citing the ministry.
sections.what_verified: No declared-tier family: TaiwanPlus has NO declared tier in the registry and counts toward NOTHING. The underlying source is the ministry itself (primary data), which is why this sig-2 item passes as a primary-source claim rather than as multi-family corroboration.
sections.what_disputed: No Chinese statement on this specific sortie count appeared in the reports checked; sortie counts alone do not establish intent (exercise, patrol, or signalling are all compatible with the numbers). A separate aggregator item citing 9 aircraft crossing the median line (via WioNews) is a different, smaller slice and must not be merged into the 49 total.
sections.why_matters: Monitor only: a 2026-high count with no incident attached. It becomes a Short only if paired with a crossing, an interception, or a political trigger.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP (TaiwanPlus published 2026-11-03T07:24Z = 11:24 , updated 09:46Z = 13:46 ; absent from all earlier Nov 3 scans) -- Taiwan defence ministry: 49 Chinese military aircraft, 6 naval vessels, 6 official ships around Taiwan Mon-Tue, a 2026 single-day high
